title: PC-CROP Federal Accounting — scoped 1C machine identity
purpose: Stack the next offline-buildable 1C connector slice on the protocol contract: a revocable machine credential whose persistent form contains no plaintext secret and is bound to one installation, one connection, one platform organization and one exact 1C legal-entity GUID. No runtime route, database persistence, vendor adapter or live claim is added.
boundaries: No apps/web, packages, lockfile, Prisma schema, migration, auth, registration, FGIS, banking, hosting or production change.
No JWT or self-asserted organization claims: the server-authoritative record is the scope and the presented secret proves only possession.
No plaintext credential is represented in the persistent record.
A credential for one 1C organization GUID never authorizes another GUID discovered in the same database.
Credential rotation creates a new secret/version; the old record is not silently extended.
The protocol parent PR remains a prerequisite; this is a stacked slice until that parent is merged.
Merge and green CI are not production acceptance.
requiredInvariants: Credential material is generated with cryptographic randomness and only a salted SHA-256 verifier belongs in persistent state.
The persistent scope is installationId + connectionId + platformOrganizationId + oneCOrganizationGuid + protocolVersion.
Expected request scope must exactly match all four binding dimensions and protocol version.
Revoked, expired, malformed or wrong-secret credentials are denied.
A future repository can revoke immediately without waiting for secret expiry because authorization reads the server-side record on every request.
requiredChecks: existing PC-CROP accounting and security gates
